title: Verify OpenNext Durable Object queue export after Cloudflare failover
description: Wrangler deploy warned that DOQueueHandler was not exported from the Worker, although .open-next/worker.js exports it and all workers.dev routes passed. Verify on-demand revalidation after cutover and fix bundling/export if queue errors appear.

title: Monitor Workers Free limits during failover
description: Workers Free was selected for the Cloudflare failover. Monitor requests/day against 100,000 and CPU per request against 10 ms; upgrade to Workers Paid if either approaches its limit.
notes: Telemetry review found Workers Observability Free with sample_rate=1 and a 200,000 events/day cap. A 24h sample showed ~387 requests, avg CPU 40.5 ms, p99 390 ms, max 509 ms; a later 1h probe showed 619 requests. The observed CPU metric is above the assumed 10 ms Free limit, so interpretation/billing needs verification. Use just cf-tail, just cf-tail-errors, just cf-deployments, and just cf-versions during monitoring.

title: Add Wrangler troubleshooting recipes to justfile

notes: Added just recipes in root justfile: cf-tail, cf-tail-errors, cf-deployments (wrangler deployments list), cf-versions, and cf-deploy-debug. All run from frontend-app and pass --env-file /dev/null. Verified with just --list, just --dry-run, and live read-only cf-deployments/cf-versions runs.
close_reason: Wrangler troubleshooting recipes added and verified.

title: Temporary Cloudflare Workers failover for medialternatives
description: Deploy the existing Next.js app to Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext, validate on workers.dev, then add reversible Workers Routes for medialternatives.com and www while Vercel is disabled. Rollback by removing routes.
notes: Cutover complete: production Workers Routes added after explicit approval on Workers Free. Apex and www verified serving the Worker with no Vercel outage response. Remaining: monitor Free limits and DO queue; roll back by deleting routes when Vercel is restored.

title: Investigate Vercel Fluid CPU overage after service restored
description: Vercel reports 6h20m Fluid CPU at 93.7% of a 4h free-tier limit and production returns 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED. Need Vercel auth/telemetry, identify top CPU routes, and reduce request amplification before permanent return.
notes: Blocked on Vercel authentication/billing window reset; no route-level CPU data available from CLI here.
